fundamentals.name: Datadog, Inc.
fundamentals.longBusinessSummary: Datadog, Inc. operates an observability and security platform for cloud applications in the United States and internationally. The company's products comprise infrastructure and application performance monitoring, log management, observability pipelines, synthetics, real user monitoring, product analytics, continuous profiler, database monitoring, data observability, LLM observability, error tracking, network monitoring, incident response, workflow automation and App builder, event management, bits AI SRE, cloud cost management, cloud security, code security, cloud SIEM, threat management, sensitive data scanner, and CI visibility. Datadog, Inc. was incorporated in 2010 and is headquartered in New York, New York.

judgment.summary: High-growth company with strong revenue and earnings expansion, but trades at a premium valuation and has thin operating margins.
judgment.earningsRecap: Last quarter beat EPS estimates by 18.3%; next earnings date is 2026-08-06.
positives: Revenue growth 32.2% YoY and quarterly earnings growth 113.4% indicate strong business momentum.
Gross margin of 79.9% is best-in-class, supporting high revenue growth.
Forward P/E of 80.82 is high but reasonable given the robust earnings growth (PEG ratio 1.42).
Strong free cash flow of $936.73M TTM provides financial flexibility.
Analyst consensus is 'strong_buy' with a mean target above the current price.
negatives: Trailing P/E of 575.42 and Price/Sales of 22.31 indicate a very high valuation.
Operating margin of 0.8% and Profit margin of 3.7% are thin despite high gross margins, suggesting high operating expenses.
Return on equity of 3.9% and Return on assets of -0.2% are weak.
Insider sell by David Galloreese, though specific impact is unclear.
Analyst questions regarding AI revenue opportunity and GPU monitoring.

news.paragraph: Datadog's stock recently broke above its 20-day moving average, coinciding with a price target boost from Benchmark to $260 and a maintained target of $230 from Macquarie. However, an insider sell by David Galloreese and a Zacks article questioning the AI revenue opportunity add some caution. The company's ability to leverage GPU monitoring for AI growth remains a key focus for investors.
